newsitem.title: UK: Britain loses tax ruling on private health care.
newsitem.headline: Britain loses tax ruling on private health care.

text.p: Britain's Customs and Excise department confirmed on Thursday it had lost an appeal court ruling concerning the VAT (Value Added Tax) status of some private medical health care provision.
But a spokesman for Customs and Excise said in an interview it would be petitioning for another hearing and was considering legislative changes to plug the loophole.
"We have lost on a two-to-one split decision. We will definitely be petitioning the House of Lords for another hearing. We will consider legislative changes," he said.

The judgement, which says supplies of drugs and implants, such as hip-replacements, should be zero-rated for VAT purposes, has important implications for the cost of private medical care and health insurance in Britain, Patrick Walker, VAT head at accountants Kidsons Impey, told Reuters.

Kidsons Impey represented Columbia Health Ltd, which runs the Wellington Hospital and other private hospitals in Britain, and brought the case. "The impact on the customer is they will not have to cope with an extra cost," Walker said.

Customs and Excise stressed the decision, which means the private health care provider can claim back VAT, would not have any implications for the National Health Service, which provides state health care to the British population.
But the ruling could lead to a potential loss of revenue if it is not overturned or legislative changes made.

"Potentially there is quite a lot of revenue at stake, around 300 million pounds ($490.3 million) a year is the sort of revenue at risk from all the private hospitals (in Britain)," the spokesman said. But he said it was "highly unlikely" that this would be the case as a change in legislation would be put forward.
"There is no political consensus for private health care to have tax breaks," he added. ($1=.6119 Pound)
